newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico seeks arrest of Iusacell's Peralta.
newsitem.headline: Mexico seeks arrest of Iusacell's Peralta.

text.p: Mexican authorities on Sunday said they were seeking the arrest of Carlos Peralta Quintero, one of the owners of cellular phone company Iusacell, on tax fraud charges.

The Finance Ministry said it had made a formal petition to the Attorney General's Office to arrest Peralta on charges he underreported his income between 1992-1995, adding it was now up to a judge to decide whether to issue an arrest warrant.

"It was discovered that in the fiscal years 1992 to 1995, he declared income less than that he really received, which he deposited in different bank investment accounts at home and abroad," a joint statement from the Finance Ministry and the Attorney General's Office said.

It said though the accounts notched up interest and foreign exchange gains, no tax was paid on them, bilking the taxman of some 11.72 million pesos. Bringing that figure up to date and including fines, Peralta owes some 40 million pesos, it said.

Peralta's tax returns have been under scrutiny by auditors since last year, and he had been in the headlines because of a controversial payment of $50 million he admits he made to Ral Salinas, jailed brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas.

He recently surrendered management control of Iusacell to Bell Atlantic, which owns 42 percent of the company, but the Peralta family continues to hold 48 percent of its shares via its Grupo Iusa holding company.
Peralta was vice-chairman of Iusacell until he was replaced by Bell Atlantic's Lawrence Babbio last November. At that time, Iusacell said Peralta was remaining on the board.
Peralta and his spokeswoman were not immediately available for comment on Sunday, an official at the company said.
